findings.ref: staged Resolver (declared output), _target_escapes_via_symlink -- READ CONTAINMENT clause
findings.note: The round-17 read-escape fix is under-scoped. It refuses a leaf symlink only when os.path.realpath(target) is not contained in repo_root. The boundary it cites is requirements.md:1304-1311 (never invokes a Provider API, READS A CREDENTIAL, or writes outside a fixed set), which is not a repository-containment rule. A committed leaf symlink at a publication target pointing at an in-repo file that is not in the authorized read set -- an untracked .env in the working tree, or a git config holding a token -- still passes the guard, and Prepare then reads it with _live_bytes and copies the referent bytes into the batch pre-image directory; on the rollback path the suite itself exercises (post-publication mismatch), _restore_to_pre writes those bytes into the git-tracked artifact path via os.replace. That is the same disclosure primitive the round closed, with the referent moved one directory inside repo_root. The machinery for the tighter rule already exists (_allowed_publication_targets_real), so the natural predicate -- the referent must be the lexical target itself or inside the feature directory -- was available. No fixture covers an in-repo, out-of-set referent: the round-15 case (run_t007_leaf_symlink_target_case) points at a sibling inside the same feature directory, and the round-17 case (run_t007_leaf_symlink_escape_case) points outside the repository; the whole middle band is unguarded and untested.

findings.ref: staged Resolver (declared output), _write_evidence -> _target_escapes_via_symlink; investigation.md section 'Rulings (a) and (b)'
findings.note: The new read-containment clause was placed inside a predicate with three call sites, and it is wrong at one of them. _write_evidence consults _target_escapes_via_symlink before the direct temp+fsync+rename Block Evidence write. That path performs NO read of the target (there is no pre-image capture on the direct route) and its write cannot escape, because os.replace replaces the entry rather than following it. So the new clause buys nothing there and costs the Block record: a leaf symlink at the feature's resolver-evidence path whose referent leaves the repository now raises EvidenceTargetUncontained, _block_reporting returns wrote_evidence=False, no Evidence is emitted, and on the two post-publication branches the journal is additionally retained into the manual-intervention state. investigation.md records the owner's ruled interaction verbatim: '(b) shrinks (a)s reach to the irreducible case. A symlink at resolver-evidence.yaml itself no longer suppresses Evidence; what remains is a feature directory that genuinely resolves outside the tree.' Round 17 re-expands the owner-accepted third AC-012 exception to a fourth condition without a ruling. It is disclosed nowhere -- not in the contract comment, not in the implementation report -- and no fixture places a symlink at that target (the only symlinked-feature-directory fixture, run_t007_staging_symlink_case, exercises the irreducible case that ruling (a) already covers).

findings.ref: verification/T-007/mutation-proofs.log -- MUTANT K; block-check driver, run_t007_leaf_symlink_escape_case
findings.note: Mutant K is the sole non-vacuity proof for this round's headline security fix, and its capture carries only 'RESULT: 373 passed, 1 failed'. Mutants A, B, C, E and G each print the FAIL lines that identify the killed assertions; K, with a single failure, prints none, so which of the fixture's five assertions the mutant kills is inferred from the tally rather than shown. The inference is weakened by the fixture's own Block assertion, which requires only returncode==1 and a stderr prefix of 'capability-resolver: ' without pinning the diagnostic id -- so that assertion cannot distinguish reaching the publication transaction from Blocking earlier for an unrelated reason. Print the FAIL line for K, and pin the id.

Four counts in the implementation report are provably wrong against artifacts the bundle itself carries. (1) The round-16 correction note states that grep -c of the run_t007_ definition prefix 'reports twelve'; the bundled driver has THIRTEEN (round 17 added run_t007_leaf_symlink_escape_case and the note was not recounted) -- a stale count inside the paragraph added to stop stale counts. (2) The same paragraph corrects the fixture-directory count to eleven, which matches the declared outputs, but leaves the sibling sentences 'ten run_t007_* functions' and 'Ten new fixtures' standing uncorrected two and twelve lines away -- the amendment-propagation class this very report names. (3) 'The figures below are from the current 369-check harness' sits directly above a control of 374. (4) 'After the proofs the real tree was re-run: 306/0 both runtimes' -- 306 is round 1s superseded green; the shipped green is 374/0 in all four captures. The substantive restoration claim is independently verifiable (the mutation log's restored sha256 ce6772bb... equals the manifest row for the staged Resolver), so this is report accuracy rather than evidence failure.

Item 1 still directs the gate reviewer at 'routing Block-path Evidence through the transaction -- that is the change with the widest blast radius (every one of the 256 pre-existing checks exercises it)' and at design.md:1201-1226 and :1257-1262. The same report withdraws that route at lines 22042-22057: round 5 reversed it, the shipped code writes Evidence directly with no staging area and no journal, and the report calls those design.md sentences 'the stale siblings inside a frozen document, not the contract the implementation follows'. The withdrawal note claims all four affected sites were corrected together; this fifth site was missed, and it is the one that steers the gate reviewer's attention. '256 pre-existing checks' is also stale against 374.

The nonce/batch-directory binding (a round-9 security guard in _read_journal) is UNCOVERED, honestly labelled, with the missing fixture named. Unlike mutant F, no impossibility is argued and none holds: the suite already ships plant_journal, and a planted all-PRE journal whose recorded nonce differs from its containing directory name flips the observable outcome from a publication-journal-recovery Block to a SAFE abandonment plus a clean exit 0. Round 15 had to retract an identical uncovered claim in this same log after a panel slot pointed out the hook already existed. F's justification, by contrast, I checked and accept: every route I could construct to a failed Evidence write fails during Prepare, before any rename, so committed==0 and the combination F needs does not arise.
